problems.description: Test fixture mutates os.environ['DATABASE'] and the module-level app_module.DATABASE but never restores them after the test, which could leak state into other tests in the same process.
The app module is imported twice (module-level `from app import ...` plus `import app as app_module`) in the fixture, a redundant workaround for how the app reads its DATABASE config.
SonarQube reports +8 cognitive complexity, all of it in test scaffolding (fixture + test methods); acceptable but worth noting.

strengths: Fixes a genuine bug: new tasks were created with status 'done' instead of 'pending'.
Comprehensive coverage of all endpoints (create/list/get/update) including success and error paths (empty/missing/whitespace title, 404s).
Per-test temp SQLite DB gives test isolation and clean teardown.
SonarQube delta is clean: +0 bugs, +0 smells, +0.0% duplications.
Follows standard Flask test_client + pytest fixture conventions.
commit_reviews.summary: A tight, correct bug-fix-plus-tests commit for a greenfield session that improves the codebase; the 0.77 convention score is driven almost entirely by pre-existing violations in files this commit never touches (celery_config.py, base.py, repositories, __init__.py), so the commit itself introduces essentially no new convention debt.

problems.description: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded static 'dev-secret-key' when the env var is unset, leaving JWT signing keys predictable in any deployment that forgets to set SECRET_KEY (not caught by SonarQube bugs +0).
login_required sets request.user_id on the request object; flask.g is the idiomatic per-request state carrier.

app.py: new classes should use PascalCase; note that most flagged violations (celery_config.py, __init__.py, base.py, task_repository.py, user_repository.py) live in files untouched by this diff and are pre-existing.
Cognitive complexity +37 in a single-file app; auth routes, decorator, and user/task models strain the tier-1 single-file structure.
Column migration is hand-rolled via _migrate_add_owner_id inside init_db; pragmatic for a seed app but not a durable migration strategy.
datetime.utcnow() is deprecated in Python 3.12+; prefer datetime.now(timezone.utc).
Adds jwt and bcrypt imports; diff truncates before requirements changes, so pinning is unverified.

strengths: Owner-scoped task queries (get_tasks/get_task/update_task filter by owner_id) prevent cross-user data access (IDOR).
Removes dead code: fetch_task alias, _legacy_format_date, _notify_admin stub.
Reuses existing module-level function + section-header conventions and the get_db()/init_db() connection pattern.
bcrypt password hashing with per-user salts; login_required preserves metadata via functools.wraps.
SonarQube: bugs +0, smells -3, duplications 0.0%.
commit_reviews.summary: Well-scoped feature addition that adds per-user auth, scopes all task queries by owner_id, and removes dead code (smells -3), at the cost of a hardcoded SECRET_KEY fallback and +37 cognitive complexity; the 0.77 convention score is skewed by pre-existing violations in files this diff never touches.

problems.description: edit_task removed the post-update `if task is None: return 404` guard and now indexes `task["status"]` directly; if update_task returns None (e.g., task deleted in a race between the get_task pre-check and the update), this raises TypeError -> 500 instead of the prior 404.

Status-transition detection and side-effect dispatch (email on completed) are embedded directly in the edit_task route handler rather than a service layer, adding branching to the endpoint (reflected in +6 smells / +17 cognitive complexity).

The `try/except ImportError` around the celery_config import fails silent: a missing or misconfigured Celery/Redis silently disables notifications with no log or surfaced error, which can mask production misconfiguration.
No test covers the fallback paths (empty email, send_notification_email being None) nor email format validation in register, so the graceful-degradation branch is untested.

strengths: Migration helper `_migrate_add_email` mirrors the existing `_migrate_add_owner_id` pattern exactly (PRAGMA column check + ALTER + commit), respecting the established DB migration convention.
The optional-import seam keeps the app and tests runnable without Celery/Redis while degrading gracefully to no-op.
Solid transition-focused tests (completion fires, non-completion and title-only updates don't), using a patched task so no broker is needed in CI.
The Celery task is routed to a dedicated `email` queue via task_routes, a clean, conventional async-integration design.
commit_reviews.summary: Discrepancy flagged: mechanical convention score 0.77 is dragged down by violations in files this commit does not touch (base.py, task_repository.py, user_repository.py, __init__.py) and apparently spurious PascalCase flags on app.py/celery_config.py (no classes defined); the commit's own new code adheres to snake_case/UPPER_CASE conventions, hence the slightly higher 0.82.

problems.description: bcrypt password verification is domain logic, not persistence, yet it sits on UserRepository and is invoked statically as UserRepository.verify_password(...) instead of via the repository instance, which is inconsistent with the instance-based repository usage elsewhere.
task_repo and user_repo are module-level singletons bound to app.py's get_db factory at import time, coupling repositories to the Flask app lifecycle and hampering dependency injection in tests.

Convention score 0.77 with 9 violations (PascalCase classes, UPPER_CASE constants); several are reported against files not touched in this diff (app.py, celery_config.py), so some appear pre-existing rather than introduced.
No test changes accompany the refactor of auth/persistence logic.

strengths: Extracts persistence into UserRepository/TaskRepository over a shared BaseRepository base, giving app.py a clean repository layer and slimming it by ~100 lines.
Net -3 SonarQube smells with 0 new bugs and 0% duplication; the diff is a straightforward move of model functions into repository classes.
New method names (create, find_by_username, find_by_id_and_owner, update) map one-to-one from the removed model functions, preserving intent and easing migration.
commit_reviews.summary: A clean repository-layer refactor that improves separation of concerns and reduces smells, with minor concerns over static password-verification placement and module-level repository singletons.

problems.description: GET /tasks response shape changed from a bare JSON list to {data, next_cursor, total} — a backward-incompatible API contract change with no versioning or deprecation path.
app.py _get_rate_limit_key inlines JWT decoding logic that duplicates the existing auth flow instead of reusing a helper, and swallows all errors with a bare 'except Exception: pass'.
Rate limiter defaults to redis://localhost:6379; production requests will fail at runtime if Redis is not deployed, and this is only masked in tests by the memory:// override.
COUNT(*) is executed on every page request to return total; acceptable now but may become expensive at scale.

The 0.77 convention score (9 violations: PascalCase/snake_case/UPPER_CASE) reflects pre-existing issues in files this commit did not touch (celery_config.py, base.py, __init__.py, user_repository.py) — this commit itself adds no new violations.

strengths: Cursor/keyset pagination using id < cursor ORDER BY id DESC scales better than OFFSET, with correct has_more detection via the limit+1 fetch.
Per-user rate limiting keyed on the JWT user_id rather than just IP gives finer-grained control.
429 error handler returns a proper Retry-After header.
New repository method find_all_by_owner_paginated follows the existing BaseRepository/_get_db pattern.
Comprehensive test updates plus a new TestPagination class; limiter safely disabled (memory:// storage, limiter.enabled = False) so tests stay deterministic.
commit_reviews.summary: Well-integrated, well-tested addition of cursor pagination and per-user rate limiting that respects existing repository and test patterns, marred only by a breaking response-shape change and the inline JWT-decode helper in app.py.

compounding_issues: Committed __pycache__/*.pyc binaries tracked in git across all sessions (10 compiled artifacts in the tree), accumulating repo noise with every commit

Ad-hoc in-code ALTER TABLE migrations (_migrate_add_owner_id, _migrate_add_email) instead of a proper migration framework; each schema change added a runtime patch and the email column required a NOT NULL DEFAULT '' backfill for pre-existing rows

Session 2 embedded all data access as module-level functions in app.py, forcing session 4 to perform a large (~150-line) extraction into repositories with no change in behavior, and leaving module-level task_repo/user_repo singletons as a coupling point
Celery notification integration gated behind try/except ImportError, silently degrading to no-op notifications if the dependency is absent
Session 5's rate limiter was initially misconfigured (default_limits instead of application_limits), requiring a follow-up 'continued' fix commit
key_decisions: Adopting JWT auth with per-user task ownership (owner_id foreign key) in session 2 — the foundational seam that every later session (notifications, refactor, rate limiting, pagination) builds on
Adding bcrypt password hashing for user credentials
Integrating Celery + Redis for async email notifications on task completion (session 3), guarded by an import fallback
Extracting an ABC BaseRepository with TaskRepository/UserRepository (session 4), which cleanly hosted the cursor-based pagination and rate-limit integration added in session 5
Introducing cross-cutting concerns in session 5: flask_limiter with a JWT-aware key function over Redis storage, plus a paginated data/next_cursor/total response envelope
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across all six commits. Test coverage grew monotonically (12 → 28 → 32 → 32 → 47 tests) with all 47 passing at the final state. app.py shrank from ~146 lines with dead stubs to 223 modular lines — net the file stayed compact while functionality expanded into dedicated repositories, celery_config, and a paginated/rate-limited API. The arc moved cleanly from a single-file seed (with dead _legacy_format_date/_notify_admin stubs, since removed) through greenfield test wiring, a feature-complete auth layer, async integration, a repository refactor, and finally cross-cutting hardening. The only quality regressions were hygiene artifacts: committed .pyc files persisted throughout, and the rate-limiter misconfiguration in the first session-5 commit was corrected in the follow-up commit.
story_review.summary: A coherent, quality-improving multi-session progression (greenfield → auth feature → async integration → repository refactor → cross-cutting hardening) that ended feature-complete with 47 passing tests, marred only by committed __pycache__ artifacts and ad-hoc SQLite migrations.
